title: Verifying That A* with an Admissible Heuristic Matches Dijkstra's Cost
description: Define the graph goal "F" and Euclidean heuristic h_euclid, run astar with h_zero (Dijkstra), and verify that ih["cost"] and i0["cost"] are equal.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Set `goal = "F"`, define `is_goal_graph(n)` to test `n == goal`, and define `h_euclid(n)` to compute the straight-line Euclidean distance `math.hypot(x - gx, y - gy)` between `coords[n]` and `coords[goal]`.

Store the A* result `(path_h, info_h)` in `(ph, ih)`, run `astar("A", ..., h_zero, debug=False)` to get the zero-heuristic (Dijkstra) result `(p0, i0)`, and check whether their path costs match within `1e-9`.

Compare `ih` (using straight-line heuristic `h_euclid`) with `i0` (using `h_zero`). `math.hypot(x - gx, y - gy)` never overestimates road distance on the graph. Both searches must therefore find a path of the same optimal cost.

steps.question: Does `abs(ih["cost"] - i0["cost"]) < 1e-9` evaluate to `True` or `False`, and what optimal path cost do both A* and Dijkstra find from `"A"` to `"F"`?
steps.answer: It evaluates to `True`, because both A* with `h_euclid` and A* with `h_zero` (Dijkstra) find the optimal cost `6.6`.

steps.description: Line 11 runs `astar` from `"A"` to `"F"` with heuristic `h_zero`.
Line 12 prints `Costs equal? True  | cost(A*,h): 6.6  cost(Dijkstra): 6.6`.
